one_liner: Research-grade MPFR-based split-radix FFT in C that runs faster than Mathematica and MATLAB/Advanpix multiprecision FFTs.
what_it_does: Computes a forward 1D complex-to-complex FFT of power-of-two length on mpfr_t arrays at any binary precision, serially or with OpenMP on 4 threads. It is a benchmark program, not a library: mpFFT.c #includes one lab kernel file (lab/serial/mp/serial_mp_fft3.c or lab/parallel/mp/parallel_mp_fft2.c), length N and precision P are compile-time macros, and data lives in global split-format arrays (inr, ini, outr, outi). To use it you lift the kernel mp_sr24_cp_fft(n, stride, sign, inr, ini, outr, outi) plus the twiddle-table setup lut() into your own code.
how_it_is_fast: It cuts the number of multiprecision multiplications, which dominate cost at high precision: a recursive decimation-in-time conjugate-pair split-radix-2/4 FFT (Yavne / Duhamel-Hollmann family) with the 3-multiply/3-add complex product (3m3a) using precomputed cos, cos+sin and cos-sin twiddle tables, hard-coded n = 1, 2, 4 base cases and a special butterfly at k = n/8; at P = 1024 bits, N = 1024 the 3m3a scheme drops multiplications from 9,336 to 7,172 and time from 3.32 ms to 3.02 ms (lab OPTIONS.md). The recursive depth-first order removes the bit-reversal pass and keeps the working set local. The parallel version only splits the inner butterfly loop of each recursion level (n >= 16) across 4 OpenMP threads; all arithmetic is plain MPFR calls, so per-operation speed is MPFR's.
when_to_use: You need a forward complex FFT at hundreds to about a million decimal digits in C and currently call Mathematica or MATLAB with the Advanpix toolbox for it.
Power-of-two lengths from 16 to about 1M points at fixed high precision (the dP = 1024 plots show it about 3x ahead of both baselines across that whole range).
You already hold data as mpfr_t and want a small, readable split-radix kernel to vendor and adapt (Apache-2.0).
Studying multiprecision FFT design trade-offs: the lab/ tree keeps several kernel variants, complexity counters and an inverse-FFT error test.
when_not_to_use: You need a library API: there is no init/plan/execute interface, N and P are #defines, and state is global, so each size/precision is a recompile.
Non-power-of-two lengths, real-input, inverse or multidimensional transforms: none are implemented (the README only describes how they could be derived).
You need rigorous error bounds or arbitrary lengths: FLINT's acb_dft does ball arithmetic and supports any length (naive, CRT, cyclic, radix-2, Bluestein).

Precision near double-double or quad-double (about 32-64 digits): at 16 digits mpFFT is only about 2x ahead of MATLAB/Advanpix in its own plot, and hardware-double-based formats are a better fit there.
Production use: single 2021 commit, self-described as 'still in development and far from complete', no tests or CI, no open issues or releases.

integration.dependencies: MPFR (4.1.0 used; mpfr_get_str_ndigits needs 4.1+), GMP (6.2.1 used), libm; OpenMP and pthread for the parallel kernel; MPFR must be built with --enable-thread-safe for parallel runs
integration.min_toolchain: C with GCC; only gcc 9.3.0 -O3 is documented
integration.platforms: POSIX (uses clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC)); tested only on an Intel Core i5-6500; others not documented
integration.thread_safety: Not reentrant: twiddle tables, input/output arrays and the serial kernel's temporaries are file-scope statics, so only one transform can run per process; the parallel kernel uses per-thread temporaries inside its own OpenMP regions.

gotchas: The shipped mpFFT.c defaults are not the benchmark configuration: CC = 1 turns on operation counters (inside '#pragma omp critical' in the parallel kernel), CH = 1 runs an O(N^2) double-precision DFT check, IN = 2 uses a fixed input rather than the random input in the plots, and M = 1; set CC 0 and CH 0 before timing.
Benchmarks time the FFT kernel only; building the twiddle table (N/4 mpfr_cos and mpfr_sin calls at full precision) and allocation are excluded and can dominate a one-off transform at high precision.

The parallel kernel hard-codes num_threads(4) and opens a new OpenMP region (with fresh mpfr_inits2 temporaries) at every recursion level with n >= 16; the author notes at best about 3x on 4 cores because only the inner loop is parallel.
Conjugate-pair recursion indexes the input through negative offsets (inr - s, wrapped by s0 = N), so the input arrays must follow the exact layout the kernel expects.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over FLINT's acb_dft when you only need a plain power-of-two forward FFT on mpfr_t values and want MPFR semantics rather than ball arithmetic, accepting that no head-to-head with FLINT exists. Unlike MPLAPACK or APFP, which speed up multiprecision linear algebra, it is the only catalogued entry aimed at the FFT itself.
verified_claims_summary: First-party plots on one Intel Core i5-6500 inside an Ubuntu 20.04 VMware Workstation VM (gcc 9.3.0 -O3, static MPFR 4.1.0 / GMP 6.2.1) time the kernel alone for a length-1024 random complex FFT: serially at 1,048,576 digits about 110 s versus about 250 s for Mathematica 11.1 and about 1,300 s for MATLAB 2019a with Advanpix, narrowing to about 2x over MATLAB at 16 digits; at fixed 1024 digits it is about 3x faster than both across lengths 16 to 1,048,576, and on 4 cores about 2-3x faster than MATLAB/Advanpix (all values read from log-scale plots, derived from page data). Baseline scripts are not in the repository, so the comparison cannot be rerun from it.
status_note: Abandoned after a single commit on 2021-10-10, but the code is Apache-2.0 (docs CC BY 4.0) and the kernel is small enough to vendor and adapt.
